item.title: Meta Settlement: Facebook and Instagram Parent Does Right Thing for Teens
item.description: Finally, what some said could never be done has happened: Meta Platforms Inc. has been forced to make real changes to protect the millions of young people who use its products. Make no mistake, while the amount that the company agreed to pay to settle a lawsuit brought by several states — up to $18 billion — is large, it is dwarfed in significance by the long-tail positive effects this so-called Big Tobacco moment will have on the well-being of teens. item.title: The Fed’s Dollar Power Comes With a Diplomatic Price
item.description: The ability and willingness of central banks to be forces for global stability will be tested with frequency in coming decades. None is likely to be challenged as much as the Federal Reserve. Such is the burden of the US possessing the world’s primary reserve currency. But is it ready for a more contentious period of statecraft?
item.dc:creator: Daniel Moss

item.title: Graham’s South Carolina Win Shows Trump Still Holds His Base
item.description: Darline Graham, sister to former South Carolina Senator Lindsey Graham, romped to victory Tuesday over Republican Congressman Ralph Norman, a MAGA conservative, on the strength of her family name and the president’s aggressive push. She now faces Democrat Annie Andrews, a Charleston pediatrician, in the reliably red state.
item.dc:creator: Mary Ellen Klas

item.title: US-Canada Tariffs Are a Sideshow to the Real Trade Risks
item.description: After US-Canada trade talks collapsed Friday, the United States imposed a 50% tariff on a long list of Canadian goods via the never-used Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer went on TV first thing Monday in an attempt to calm financial markets with some basic tariff math. He said the new action hits a small percentage of Canadian imports into the US and an even smaller share of consumption, so there’s “no possible way it can really affect US well-being.”
item.dc:creator: Scott Lincicome

item.title: Scott Bessent's Bond Moves Won't Get the US Out of Fiscal Trouble
item.description: The US government, steward of the world’s largest economy, faces a darkening fiscal outlook as sovereign borrowing costs surge. Unfortunately, it seems intent on trying any fix except the one that might help.
item.dc:creator: The Editors

item.title: Extreme Heat Hurts Student Learning and Health
item.description: Each year, schools around the country spend the last weeks of summer break preparing for the day when promising young minds flood through their doors. Yet educators and policymakers too often overlook a crucial step in helping children thrive: developing a plan for extreme heat.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Jarvis

item.title: Bitcoin: The Bessent Bounce Does Not Tell the Full Story
item.description: Bitcoin just notched its biggest weekly gain in more than three years, putting an end to a summer of stagnation. Crypto traders can thank US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, whose plan to boost bond buybacks spurred the move. But it’ll take more than that to return this market to genuinely bullish territory.
item.dc:creator: Emily Nicolle

item.title: To Working-Class Voters, Affordability Isn't Just About Costs
item.description: Democrats’ obsession with “affordability” is right on target, given that American workers’ share of GDP is near the lowest ever recorded. Today, 61% of Americans are skimping at the grocery store, and housing and childcare are unaffordable even for many college grads. item.dc:creator: Joan C. Williams and Jared Abbott

item.title: United Airlines Expands International Routes With Southwest Model
item.description: Got your bags packed for Ljubljana? Plan to spend some vacation days in Olbia? United Airlines Holdings Inc. will whisk you there nonstop from Newark starting next summer.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Black

item.title: Harry and Meghan Are Already Annoying British Taxpayers
item.description: Six years on from their dramatic UK departure, Prince Harry and his wife Meghan are returning from California with their two small children. Royal watchers have many questions: Where will they live and where will Archie and Lilibet go to school? What does this say about Harry’s strained relationship with his father King Charles and brother William? And can Meghan forgive William’s wife Catherine after they fell out over whether the latter’s daughter wore tights to Harry’s wedding?
item.dc:creator: Rosa Prince

item.title: AI Models: Nvidia Is Jolting Silicon Valley to Think Like China
item.description: When a typical business finds its supply chain costs have risen, it will absorb the increase to keep its customers happy. Nvidia isn’t a typical business. It enjoys gross profit margins of 75% and commands between 70% and 90% of the global market for artificial-intelligence chips. So when the companies that make memory components put their prices up, Nvidia passed the hike on. item.title: L3Harris Should Have Known Better When It Hired Its CEO
item.description: L3Harris should have known it was getting damaged goods when it hired Christopher Kubasik.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Karl

item.title: Ambani’s Succession Plan Confronts a Wildlife Problem
item.description: Asia’s second-richest business clan just made a highly public commitment to rein in its youngest scion’s passion project, a controversial wildlife sanctuary. In doing so, tycoon Mukesh Ambani is cutting the risks to his empire and ironing out a major wrinkle in his succession plans.
